transcript:
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Kyle Snyder.
President Trump has released what the White House says is a voluntary accord with major
tech companies on artificial intelligence, saying they've agreed to self-police AI development.
Trump unveiled a one-page document on social media after meeting with tech executives for
a Tuesday lunch at the White House.
The agreement comes amid alarm bells sounded by AI executives who have called on the government
to establish guardrails.
OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, among the tech leaders calling for guardrails in his company, was
among those that signed the agreement.
Altman himself was in San Francisco Tuesday unveiling new products at the company's dev
day event from member station KQED, Rachel Myro reports.
Outside the event, protesters demanded OpenAI stop working with the military and ICE.
Inside, one product was missing, GPT 6.1.
OpenAI held back its release of the model after tests found the model overstepped its
authority and misreported what it had done.
Instead, Altman pitched dots, always on AI agents designed to act before you ask.
It can hugely magnify your ability and expand your potential, working 24/7 to take on things
that you don't want to do so you can focus on higher-level work.
Back in Washington, D.C., President Trump brushed off calls for new guardrails, saying
the industry should regulate itself.
For NPR News, I'm Rachel Myro.
Special Counsel Jack Smith on Capitol Hill Tuesday appearing before the Senate Judiciary
Committee where he defended his prosecutions of Donald Trump and pushed back against Republican
efforts to paint him and his team as partisan.
My service has spanned both Republican and Democratic administrations.
I am not a politician and I have no partisan loyalty.
My career has been dedicated to serving our country by upholding the rule of law and the
core principles upon which our country was founded.
Republicans on the panel claim Smith's investigative tactics were not ethical.
Officials at Cornell University facing growing criticism over their handling of an alleged
rape case in 2024.
New York Governor Kathy Hochul calling for an independent investigation.
Here's NPR's Brian Mann.
Hochul called a woman's account of being drugged and gang-raped at Cornell in 2024 horrifying.
She says there are serious questions and is calling for a transparent, independent review
of the university's response.
A local prosecutor says the alleged victim described parts of the incident as consensual
at the time, but potential evidence of violence by seven male students was only investigated
by campus police, not by city police.
Ithaca's mayor Robert Cantelmo has also blasted Cornell's response.
In a statement to NPR, Cornell University says it will work with elected officials to
address safety concerns.
They didn't say whether they will approve an independent investigation.
Ryan Mann, NPR News, Ithaca, New York.
And you're listening to NPR News.
As some states like Pennsylvania face large measles outbreaks, others have alerted the
public of possible exposures to the highly contagious virus.
NPR's Rachel Carlson has more on what travelers should know.
An exposure happens when a person comes into contact with someone who has measles, like
in California, when an infected, unvaccinated passenger traveled throughout the state on
trains and buses.
Up to nine out of 10 people exposed to measles could get sick, if they're not protected.
Dr. Paul Offit is the director of the Vaccine Education Center at the Children's Hospital
of Philadelphia.
You don't have to come in direct contact with someone who has measles to get infected.
You just have to be within their airspace within two hours of them being there.
Offit says protection in this case means being fully vaccinated with two doses of the MMR
vaccine.
That not only helps protect you, but people who can't be or aren't yet vaccinated, like
those with compromised immune systems or infants.
Rachel Carlson, NPR News.
At least for now, the Supreme Court is letting the Trump administration resume deporting people
to countries other than their own.
The court Tuesday granted the Justice Department's emergency request to put on hold a Boston
federal judge's ruling that the policy to remove migrants to third countries is unlawful.
The Supreme Court is to hear arguments in the case in December.
Asian stocks mixed in Wednesday trading, Japan's benchmarking EK up 2%, while stocks in South
Korea given up early gains after a down day on Wall Street.
I'm Jyle Snyder.
This is NPR News.

OpenAI CEO Sam Altman unveils new AI products at dev day event in San Francisco
OpenAI withholds release of GPT 6.1 model after tests found it overstepped authority
Special Counsel Jack Smith defends prosecutions of Donald Trump before Senate Judiciary Committee
Cornell University facing criticism over handling of alleged 2024 rape case, Governor Hochul calls for investigation
Pennsylvania and other states face measles outbreaks, health officials alert public to possible exposures
Supreme Court grants Trump administration request to resume deporting migrants to third countries
